title: Subset sum game
description: Generalised subset sum: pick x-numbers so that no choice of y-numbers brings the total to the target, a Sigma-2-complete problem (Berman, Karpinski, Larmore, Plandowski and Rytter). The check only needs the sum of the picked numbers, so the interface is the derived atom xsum/1, and a refinement forbids a sum together with every set that has it. Glue pick/1 instead (and mark all of it relevant) to get one refinement per set.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: The numbers and the target. Added to every solver.
fragments.text:
% Two lists of numbers and a target. The x-player picks some of the first list; then
% the y-player may add some of the second list to reach the target exactly.
xnum(1,2). xnum(2,8). xnum(3,9). xnum(4,10). xnum(5,12). xnum(6,13). xnum(7,14).
ynum(1,2). ynum(2,4). ynum(3,7). ynum(4,16). ynum(5,18). ynum(6,19). ynum(7,21).
target(71).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): any set of x-numbers, with its sum.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: any set of x-numbers.
{ pick(I) : xnum(I,_) }.
% Its sum. This derived atom is all the check needs to know.
xsum(S) :- S = #sum { W,I : pick(I), xnum(I,W) }.
#show pick/1.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the sum of the picked numbers (a derived atom).

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for y-numbers that complete the sum to the target (solver C).
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: a set of y-numbers that adds exactly the missing amount.
{ take(J) : ynum(J,_) }.
:- xsum(S), target(T), #sum { W,J : take(J), ynum(J,W) } != T - S.
#show take/1.

% It depends on the sum only: no set with this sum is a solution.
relevant(xsum(S)) :- xsum(S).

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

library.summary: Sets of x-numbers that no set of y-numbers completes to the target; the interface is the derived sum, so one clause removes all sets with that sum (7 + 7 numbers, 11 solutions).
